This mainly adds support for AutoMQM metrics, i.e., MQM-like metrics (consisting of error spans with severity/category assignments) made by AI instead of human raters. Each rater name that has the prefix "AutoMQM" is treated as a distinct metric.

- The scores table at the top shows all AutoMQM metrics.
- The visibility of MQM score slice columns can now be toggled.
- Since the scores table can get very wide, if there is more than one MQM-like metric, then we start out the details columns in hidden state.
- The visibility state of details columns persists across sorting/filtering.
- When comparing rater-specific scores, we conflate all MQM-like metrics, allowing us to compare (using histograms, significance tests) AutoMQM with MQM.
- In the examples tables, we now allow narrowing the view to just the annotations made by any specific rater by hovering the mouse over the rater's ID in the last column. Each rater has a
unique flag color associated with them, and this temporary narrowing is indicated in the UI by showing the rater's flag next to the text. You can also hover over a rater's flag to activate this narrowing.
- Split the earlier "errors" DIV into one for status and one for errors.

The other changes are around data reading:

- Instead of not loading more data after MAX_DATA_LINES lines (as was being done earlier), we now use a MAX_SEGMENTS limit (set to 10000) and ignore data from segments not in the first MAX_SEGMENTS distinct doc-segs (but we continue to load data for existing doc-segs, say from more systems/raters).
- This MAX_SEGMENTS limiting is also used to simply not remember any data lines that were not used, saving memory. Thus, when we save the data, only data for the doc-segs used is saved.

* Adds initial computation of posterior class probabilities, given prior and confusion matrix

The other ones are to make sure all posterior class probabilities add up to 1 for a given class prediction.

When the confusion matrix has no false positives (i.e. filled only on the diagonal), the posterior
for a class is simply 1 because the evidence equals the likelihood * prior.

When the confusion matrix has all-zero columns (i.e. the inner classifier fails to make any
prediction for a given class), the posterior for these classes equals their prior probability.
This is necessary to make sure that the posterior probabilities of all classes, given a
prediction, sum to 1.
